answer: A farm that wants 155 keys as a result pays 155 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the ember seed, the zephyr timing is verifiable from the thread record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 265 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
